s.H4973: contr. from 3216; properly, a biter, i.e. a tooth KJV: cheek (jaw) tooth, jaw.
s.H4974: from 8552; wholesomeness; also (adverb) completely KJV: men (by reading 4962), soundness.
s.H4975: from an unused root meaning to be slender; properly, the waist or small of the back; only in plural the loins KJV: greyhound, loins, side.
s.H4976: from 5414; a present KJV: gift, to give, reward.
s.H4977: the same as 4976; Mattan, the name of a priest of Baal, and of an Israelite KJV: Mattan.

s.H4982: from 4976; liberal; Mattenai, the name of three Israelites KJV: Mattenai.
s.H4983: or מַתַּנְיָהוּ; from 4976 and 3050; gift of Jah; Mattanjah, the name of ten Israelites KJV: Mattaniah.
s.H4984: from 5375; (used as abstractly) supreme exaltation KJV: exalted.
s.H4985: a primitive root; to suck, by implication, to relish, or (intransitively) be sweet KJV: be (made, × take) sweet.
s.H4986: from 4985; figuratively, pleasantness (of discourse) KJV: sweetness.
s.H4988: from 4985; a dainty, i.e. (generally) food KJV: feed sweetly.
s.H4989: feminine of 4987; sweetness; Mithkah, a place in the Desert KJV: Mithcah.
s.H4990: of Persian origin; Mithredath, the name of two Persians KJV: Mithredath.
s.H4991: feminine of 4976 abbreviated form; a present KJV: gift.
s.H4992: for 4993; gift of Jah; Mattattah, an Israelite KJV: Mattathah.
s.H4993: or מַתִּתְיָהוּ; from 4991 and 3050; gift of Jah; Mattithjah, the name of four Israelites KJV: Mattithiah. n
s.H4994: a primitive particle of incitement and entreaty, which may usually be rendered; 'I pray', 'now', or 'then'; added mostly to verbs (in the Imperative or Future), or to interjections, occasionally to an adverb or conjunction KJV: I beseech (pray) thee (you), go to, now, oh.
s.H4995: apparently from 5106 in the sense of harshness from refusal; properly, tough, i.e. uncooked (flesh) KJV: raw.
s.H4996: of Egyptian origin; No (i.e. Thebes), the capital of Upper Egypt KJV: No. Compare 528.
s.H4997: or נאוֹדlemma נֹאוד vowel, corrected to נאוֹדxlit nôʼwd corrected to nʼôwd; also (feminine) נֹאדָה; from an unused root of uncertain signification; a (skin or leather) bag (for fluids) KJV: bottle.
s.H4998: a primitive root; properly, to be at home, i.e. (by implication) to be pleasant (or suitable), i.e. beautiful KJV: be beautiful, become, be comely.
s.H4999: from 4998; a home; figuratively, a pasture KJV: habitation, house, pasture, pleasant place.
